    Wednesday 16 September 2026

    Morning briefing

    Morning briefing

    The book refuses to fill itself: eight of ten option slots ship as declared vacancies at size zero, because only two contracts on the whole board sit inside the required-move gate and the chair may drop a leg but never lift one

    Executive summary

    Mandate: Mix (any). OVERNIGHT. Asia is split and half stale - Hang Seng +0.19% and Shanghai +0.71% closed higher, while Nikkei 225 -0.01% and KOSPI -0.85% are stale bars from 2026-09-15 - Europe is in session and uniformly bid (FTSE +0.38%, DAX +0.73%, Euro Stoxx +0.70%), and the US futures are carrying the news hardest with S&P 500 futures +1.32% and Nasdaq 100 futures +1.95%, against a 10-year at 4.96 (-0.78%) and a flat dollar at 99.65. Europe and the futures agree on direction; Asia's two live closes agree and its two stale rows do not, so the agreement is thinner than the +1.64% futures average makes it look. Expected shape: a morning move that retraces and then reclaims - a 1.9% Nasdaq gap into SPY that is -0.25% over five days, VIX 16.65 and rising, and an FFT composite projecting -0.50% over the next ten sessions is a gap that gets sold before it is bought back.

    THE SHEET'S ORGANISING SIGNAL IS ABSENT, MEASURED. Every thesis on this board is a flow thesis, and volume_ratio above 1.00x is served 0 of 40 - the highest participation on the sheet is AAPL at 0.49x, and the median row is nearer 0.15x. That is not a board of unusual option activity; it is forty fractions of books that already existed. I therefore grade on residual momentum, on the contract, and on the calibration-weighted room, and I cap what any 'call volume 0.4x OI' sentence can earn. That is why the top grade in this book is 62 and not 80: with the sheet's own organising signal missing on every row, no lead here has earned a conviction number, and the spread runs 62 (META) to 14 (SBUX) so the ranking still means something. Contract blocks: option_contract is served non-null on 6 of 40 rows (HOOD, KLAC, ORCL, COIN, SBUX, T); the veto-clean census serves 7 of 40 names with a contract that clears DTE>=3, premium>=$0.50 and open interest>=250 (COIN, HOOD, KLAC, ORCL, TDG, TT, FANG). Ten of the forty shipped contracts were visible at grade time last night at their exact morning premium; today every contract I quote is copied from my own prompt and nothing is recalled.

    THE ARITHMETIC THAT DECIDES THE OPTION COLUMN. Ten option slots, seven veto-clean names: the column cannot be filled with certified legs, and last night's court struck promotion outright - no name is ever promoted into a column to satisfy a structure. So the option column ships SEVEN certified legs and declares THREE vacancies at stake 0.0 (T, CRWD, SBUX), which is the refusal channel my own rule requires - size zero in columns.json, merit grade left intact, no contract shipped, column still scoreable. The court's +3.0% REQMOVE gate on the top three then decides the head of the column by elimination rather than by preference: only two contracts on the entire board sit inside it, COIN at REQMOVE -5.092% and KLAC at +0.486%, so ranks one and two are the only legs the gate admits and rank three is a declared vacancy. I did not lift anything on required move and I will not - REQ is moneyness, and moneyness is variance. DIR= and REQ= ON TEN OF TEN LEGS, IN FILED ORDER. 1 COIN: DIR=highest room median 56.5, graham (best-calibrated seat, +0.122) at 88, net -6.36%, E_norm -0.148 short-aligned; REQ=-5.092 (break_even_move_pct -1.90). 2 KLAC: DIR=call_put_ratio 0.27, heaviest put skew served, -6.60% week, net -0.64%; REQ=+0.486 (break_even_move_pct -3.68). 3 T: DIR=room median 50.0, call_put_ratio 0.23, net -5.50%; REQ=-7.547 (break_even_move_pct -0.34) - VACANCY, open_interest 100 against my floor of 250. 4 TDG: DIR=E_norm -0.470, eps -0.263, rank 476/508, the strongest bear residual in the certified set, net -5.45%; REQ=+9.064. 5 TT: DIR=E_norm -0.260, rank 388/508, below both SMAs, net -3.49%; REQ=+3.866. 6 FANG: DIR=E_norm +0.264, rank 154/508, net -2.25%; REQ=+14.405. 7 HOOD: DIR=E_norm +0.148, eps +0.228, rank 148/508, net -7.82%; REQ=+6.03. 8 ORCL: DIR=E_norm -0.151, rank 294/508 - negative residual under a long, the weakest DIR certified - net -5.42%; REQ=+4.254. 9 CRWD: DIR=net +7.48% against the short, rank 164/508 against it; REQ=not served, no contract in any window - VACANCY. 10 SBUX: DIR=E_norm -0.684, rank 508/508, the market's worst residual; REQ=+14.10 (break_even_move_pct 14.34) - VACANCY, premium $0.21 against my floor of $0.50. The filed order is monotone in DIR and plainly not monotone in REQ (-5.09, +0.49, -7.55, +9.06, +3.87, +14.41, +6.03, +4.25). EXPIRY SPREAD. Seven certified legs across four distinct expiries: 2026-09-25 x3 (COIN, KLAC, HOOD), 2026-10-02 x1 (ORCL), 2026-11-20 x1 (TDG), 2026-12-18 x2 (TT, FANG). Maximum on any one date is 3 against the ceiling of 4, so R4's ceiling holds with a leg to spare and no name was moved, promoted or invented to reach a date. The three vacancies carry no expiry because they carry no contract.

    WHERE CONVICTION SITS, AND WHAT IS ONE BET WEARING SEVERAL TICKERS. The share column's conviction is mega-cap tech beta: META, AAPL and DELL are ONE bet, ranked best-expression first on residual (META rank 15/508, AAPL 42/508, DELL 101/508), and GOOGL, AMD, NVDA and AVGO are further copies that do not ship for that reason and not because they grade badly - GOOGL at 49 outranks three lines that do book. ELV and GILD are one healthcare-long pair. On the short side COST, GD and MCD are one low-volatility defensive fade, and I flag that all three carry heavy w on sigma under 1.5%/day, which the framework's division by sigma twice rewards quadratically - I have discounted them for that artefact rather than crediting the weight. In options, COIN, KLAC, TDG and TT are four expressions of one stance: short high-beta and rate-sensitive risk into a rising-VIX tape. That is not diversification, and I do not present it as such - diversification is a variance instrument and cannot change a mean. CLASS SPLIT of the Top 20: 3 intraday (AAPL, DELL, INTC), 11 swing, 5 position (GILD, COST, GD, TDG, FANG) and 1 long_term (TT) - inside the mandate's 3/8/4 target.

    WHAT WOULD INVALIDATE THE DAY. The top ideas die on one condition each, written as a close and nothing else: META below 634.44, COIN above 170.82, AAPL below 328.21, DELL below 567.29, ELV below 397.39. The regime-level kill is the shape itself - if the gap opens and never retraces, the two shorts at the head of the option column (COIN, KLAC) are wrong from the first print, and if VIX 16.65 keeps rising while the futures' +1.64% holds into the cash open, the low-volatility defensive shorts (COST, GD, MCD) are the lines that bleed first.

    RATCHETS ON THE HIGH-VARIANCE LINES, PRE-COMMITTED BEFORE THE OPEN. WDC (sigma 5.78%/day) and DELL (5.16%/day): at +1.0 ATR in favour, the stop moves to entry and half the line is retired; there is no second add. COIN and KLAC (9 DTE): at +50% on premium, half the contract is sold and the remainder runs to expiry on the house's money; at -40% on premium the leg is closed in the record the same session, because a nine-day option does not get a second thesis. TDG, TT and FANG (65-93 DTE): no ratchet before 20 sessions, then the stop is the underlying's kill level on a closing basis only. NOT BOOKED (computed as the forty named candidates minus columns.json, so its intersection with the shipped book is empty by construction): ADSK, AMD, AMGN, AMZN, AVGO, BAC, CASY, CMI, GOOGL, GS, INTC, ISRG, JBHT, MPWR, MU, NEE, NVDA, RVTY, STX, TER. Twenty names, and INTC and AMD appear here despite grading 46 and 44 - the first because a same-session line I cannot certify an option on is not worth a share slot today, the second because it is the fifth copy of a bet I already hold three times.

    PER-TICKER OPTION LINE. COIN MERIT 1 PUBLISHED 1. KLAC MERIT 2 PUBLISHED 2. T MERIT 3 PUBLISHED 3. TDG MERIT 4 PUBLISHED 4. TT MERIT 5 PUBLISHED 5. FANG MERIT 6 PUBLISHED 6. HOOD MERIT 7 PUBLISHED 7. ORCL MERIT 8 PUBLISHED 8. CRWD MERIT 9 PUBLISHED 9. SBUX MERIT 10 PUBLISHED 10. OVERRIDE count: 0.

    THE SHARE COLUMN'S PUBLISHED GRADES ARE NOT MINE. The 2026-09-11 court overwrites every share line with the room's RAW MEDIAN before persistence, and that gate moved nine of ten lines last night and beat my own grades, so I state both orderings and let the record compare them: published-by-median will read DELL 51, AAPL 50, META 50, ELV 48, DVN 48, GILD 47, MCD 45.5, WDC 44.5, COST 42.5, GD 41; my pre-gate ordering, preserved in challenger.json, is META, AAPL, DELL, ELV, DVN, GILD, COST, WDC, GD, MCD. The construction block compares against the pre-gate ordering, not against the gate's own output - a test whose two arms are the same arm is not a result.

    THE PYRAMID IS SUSPENDED. The money standings are dated 2026-09-15 and the paper league has not been marked since 2026-09-01, so there is no leader, no crown and no tie-break weight this morning, and I have not inferred one. Last night's court struck 'follow the leader' in any case: I weight each seat by its trailing within-column calibration and never by its equity. On that basis graham (+0.122), oracle (+0.092), timekeeper (+0.082) and the skeptic (+0.068) carry weight; sam (-0.284), dagger (-0.222), flow (-0.189) and domestic_desk (-0.176) are discounted toward zero rather than inverted, because a negative correlation over 300 grades is evidence that a seat's ordering is noise-plus-sign, not a licence to buy whatever it hates - the mechanical inversion of this room's grades would have shipped RVTY, CRWD, CASY and AMGN today, which is its own refutation.

    HOUSE RULES, DECIDED BEFORE THE OPEN. STAKES: share_default 1.0 unit, option_default 0.5 unit, per_line_cap 1.0, and three declared overrides at 0.0 - T, CRWD and SBUX - which are vacancies and not positions; the builder applies the default to any name it substitutes and prints the substitution by name, and if it cannot read a declaration it reports EQUAL WEIGHT rather than filling the hole silently. EXITS: every lead carries one closing-price kill and no second clause; an intraday print through a level does not fire it; the ratchets above are fixed now and are not revisited mid-session. WINDFALL: any leg that doubles on premium has half retired at once and the remainder runs on house money to expiry - the windfall is never re-risked into a new line the same session, and no stake is increased after the open for any reason.

    Live board session: fourteen graders, the Skeptic and the Executive, each a separate model call over the same forty-candidate packet, answering the app's own prompts with each seat's most recent Evening Court lessons prepended. Collector data is real and timestamped. THE PACKET FROZE AT 11:24 ET, 114 MINUTES AFTER THE OPEN - the earliest freeze of the week - so entries are mid-session marks and tonight's court scores about four and a half hours.

    What the board did not know
    1. THIRTY-FOUR OF THE FORTY CANDIDATES CAN CARRY NO ELIGIBLE CONTRACT AT ALL, and the reason is one date: their entire served chain is 2026-09-18, which is 2 DTE today and therefore barred by the standing DTE >= 3 veto. The flow the whole sheet is built on lives in an expiry the book may not buy and which dies Friday.
    2. NOT ONE OF THE FORTY ROWS CARRIES A VOLUME RATIO ABOVE 1.00. The highest on the sheet is AAPL at 0.49x and the modal row is 0.10-0.15x, so every candidate's stated thesis - 'call/put volume 0.Nx OI' - is a fraction of a book that already existed rather than fresh positioning. The Skeptic's reading, filed in full: seven of the sheet's headline call/put ratios are produced in places nobody is standing, and the loudest number on the board (DVN at 10.64) sits on a volume ratio of 0.15.
    3. THE PYRAMID IS SUSPENDED FROM EVERY PROMPT THIS SESSION. The money standings are dated 2026-09-15 and the Paper League has not been marked to market since 2026-09-01, because paper.mark_to_market is a scheduler job and the app has not run as a service. Under the 2026-09-10 court's ruling 7 a stale block is withheld rather than shipped: no leader, no crown and no tie-break weight for any seat including the chair. The chair weighted seats by trailing calibration alone, and recorded that it discounted negative-correlation seats toward zero rather than inverting them, because mechanical inversion would have shipped RVTY, CRWD, CASY and AMGN.
    4. A TWO-LEG OPTION COLUMN CANNOT BE SCORED. A rank correlation over two points is not a measurement, so tonight's court will have no readable option rho. The chair filed this against its own ruling: the gate stopped the risk by destroying the readout.
    5. NO IV LADDER IS SERVED FOR ANY CONTRACT LINE - the Skeptic's VOL tag printed NONE on all six of its contract lines and four other seats withheld an IV-slope read for the same reason.
    6. NO EARNINGS OR EVENT CALENDAR IS SERVED FOR ANY OF THE FORTY.
    7. CONGRESSIONAL DISCLOSURE PRINTED EMPTY FOR THE 24TH CONSECUTIVE SESSION - zero filings, zero buys, zero sales on all forty names.
    8. TWO OF THE ELEVEN OVERNIGHT ROWS CAME BACK STALE and are stamped and excluded from the read, which covers Asia, Europe and the futures on nine live rows.
    9. The packet ships no ATR field, so the lead brackets and several seats' risk arithmetic use a swing-range proxy over a 20-bar window, labelled as a proxy.
    10. The 11:24 ET freeze is 114 minutes into the session. Entries are mid-session marks, not opens.
    Contracts the desk could not transact
    1. expiry_concentration — ONE date, 2026-09-25, carrying both legs at 9 DTE. R4's ceiling of four is satisfied trivially; its three-expiry floor was struck last night and is reported as an advisory only on a FULL ten-leg column, which this is not. The concentration is not the chair's choice: it filed four distinct dates across seven certified legs, and the required-move gate removed five of them, all of the non-09-25 ones. A rule against concentration was handed maximum concentration by a rule against distance.
    2. reqmove_on_every_leg — KLAC +0.486%, COIN -5.092%. Those are the only two contracts on the entire forty-name board inside the +3.0% ceiling. The five dropped certified legs sat at TDG +9.064%, TT +3.866%, FANG +14.405%, HOOD +6.030% and ORCL +4.254% - named here rather than hidden, with their merit grades intact.
    3. the_option_cap — COIN was graded 58 by the chair and is capped to 55 under the W38 prospectus, which holds the priced option book UNPROVEN at a mean of -13.774% over n=7. The cap sits below the >=60 spotlight gate on purpose, so with it applied the top grade in the whole book is 55 and nothing is certified.
    4. veto_breaches_on_the_record — NONE, and the vetoes are the reason this column is two legs long. Both shipped contracts clear DTE >= 3, premium >= $0.50 and OI >= 250: KLAC at 9 DTE, $5.45, 720 open interest and COIN at 9 DTE, $11.65, 338. Three of the chair's ten named option tickers failed the vetoes outright - T at 100 open interest, SBUX at $0.21 premium, and CRWD with no contract served in any window - and were declared vacancies before the required-move gate ever reached them.

    House rules
    1. THE OPTION COLUMN SHIPS TWO LEGS AND EIGHT DECLARED VACANCIES, and that is the whole story of this session. Ten slots, seven names carrying a veto-clean contract, and of those seven only TWO sit inside the required-move gate the 2026-09-10 court set at +3.0%%. The chair's own R9 from 2026-09-14 says required move may DROP a leg and never LIFT one, so the remedy cascaded: drop the third-ranked leg and the fourth becomes third, and so on down to the two that clear. COIN at -5.092%% and KLAC at +0.486%% are the book's option column. T, TDG, TT, FANG, HOOD, ORCL, CRWD and SBUX are UNCERTIFIED VACANCIES at stake 0.0 - they ship nothing, and their merit grades stand untouched.
    2. THE CASCADE IS A PROPERTY OF THE BOARD, NOT OF THE CHAIR'S ORDERING. The chair checked: only two of the seven certified contracts sit inside +3.0%%, so NO ordering of today's certified set - its own or any other - can seat a gate-clean leg at rank three. In its words: 'there is no way out'. It declined four escapes and wrote them down - no relaxing the gate, no lifting a nearer leg, no resizing the survivors to compensate, and no moving a dropped name into the share column to rescue it.
    3. R4 SITS AS A CEILING ONLY, AMENDED OVERNIGHT. Last night's court reversed its own rule after one reading: the four-leg ceiling stands, the three-expiry floor is struck, and no name is ever promoted into a column to satisfy a date. The chair's reason was that a name reachable only on a rarely-reachable date is a name whose veto-clean contract is far from the money, so the floor had been operating as a hidden out-of-the-money filter - every promoted leg beyond 2.869%% OTM, every merit leg inside 0.771%%, no overlap, and the merit legs returned +1.755%% against -3.62%% for the forced ones.
    4. AND THE TWO GATES COLLIDED. A rule written against expiry concentration has been handed maximum concentration by a rule written against distance: both survivors expire 2026-09-25, so the column's spread collapsed from the chair's filed four dates to ONE. The ceiling of four is satisfied trivially at two legs. The chair filed that interaction for tonight's court as new and unruled.
    5. THE SHARE COLUMN SHIPS ON RAW SEAT MEDIANS, nine of its ten lines moved, every gap in the same direction: META 62 to 50, AAPL 58 to 50, DELL 57 to 47, ELV 56 to 48, DVN 52 to 46, GILD 50 to 46, COST 50 to 40, WDC 47 to 44, GD 46 to 38, with MCD the only line where chair and room already agreed. The option cap then moved COIN from 58 to 55. NO SPOTLIGHT: the top grade in the book is 55.
    6. THE SLATE IS NOW THE CHAIR'S TWO COLUMNS AND NOTHING ELSE. The builder used to fill twenty slots by grade order over all forty candidates, which is how AAPL and DECK shipped yesterday carrying no declared stake after the median rule dropped HCA and KMB. Today it would have back-filled eight share names against eight option vacancies. The book is now exactly what columns.json names.
    7. STAKES ARE A FUNCTION, NOT A LIST, on last night's R11: share_default 1.0, option_default 0.5, per_line_cap 1.0, and an override map that binds only on shipped names - which is where the eight zeroes live. The scorer reads it.
    8. Stop and target are the house bracket off the 'aggressive' risk profile - 2.0 ATR to the stop, 4.0 ATR to the target - anchored on the entry, and every lead carries the chair's kill line whose level IS the stop in the record.
